The nbfx Options API defines the annotations with which a module contributes categories and panels to the JavaFX options dialog.
The module contains the SOURCE-retention @OptionsRegistration, @OptionsSubRegistration and @OptionsContainerRegistration annotations and a LayerGeneratingProcessor that writes NbFx/Options entries into the compiling module's generated layer. The options reader consumes those entries through LayerPaths.
A module declares a top-level options category with @OptionsRegistration, a sub-panel with @OptionsSubRegistration, or an empty grouping category with @OptionsContainerRegistration.
The processor is covered by a unit test that asserts the generated layer fragments for a sample annotated source. The module API is marked under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.
A JDK is required to compile the annotation processor.
Only com.gluonhq.netbeans.nbfx.api.options is public. The processor implementation is an implementation detail and is not exported.
The processor is discovered by the compiler through the META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor service, generated by @ServiceProvider(service=Processor.class).
See lookup-lookup.
Yes. The processor creates NbFx/Options/<id>.instance, NbFx/Options/<category>/<id>.instance and NbFx/Options/<id> folder entries.

The annotation processor runs in the compiler's processing rounds and is stateless. It does not touch the JavaFX thread.
No code runs on startup; the module only contributes a compiled annotation processor.
No code runs on exit.
